I’ve done a little bit of research regarding this skip and have some examples to show.
The main takeaway is that if you collide with the wall at all, you always have at least **1 frame** in which you can press jump. How many frames you actually have depends on how far you are up. 

There will be a few example videos, the first showing a scenario in which I slide off the wall, followed by an example of getting a walljump without cling. The main thing is that the first frame you collide with the walls, and the subsequent frames you are colliding with the wall, you are able to walljump, regardless of if hornet visually shows a cling grip state or not. The second video shows a successful BS2 in which I press jump the first possible frame without clinging. 

The third video shows 3 examples, the first being pressing jump without cling on the third frame of collision. The second is of pressing jump 2f early (in a scenario in which I wouldn’t get cling), and the third is a sample cling grip. It seems if roughly half of hornets hitbox collides with the wall then she will cling.

If you cling grip you have 7 frames before downward acceleration starts, combined with the time it takes to slip off this means a clingged jump usually have at least 10f (0.167s) or so to be inputted from the wall. Conversely, in my own experience most non-clingged attempts have roughly 3-4f which you’re able to jump off of.

A lot of attempts you won’t get high enough to cling, but you will be able to hit this **3-4f window and still get the skip.**

I re-worked Scotty's version of this skip to avoid having to do the precise jump off the platform. I haven't played around with it a ton yet, but I think it has potential. Here's the steps I follow to do this:

- When jumping to the platform below the flying enemy, float underneath its aggro range to avoid waking it up.
- Dash into the wall and walljump, holding right until you're just past the background flag.
- Dash left and immediately hold right so that you begin a sprint turnaround the moment you land. You want to be fairly far right on the platform so you're close enough to cause the flying enemy to away, to the right.
- Sprint jump a moment after landing, aiming to jump over the flying enemy.
- If you clear the flying enemy, turn around and pogo it. You should pogo the top of its hitbox, not the side. If you jump into the enemy and get hit, you can still pogo it and make it to the right side. You can also make this step easier by hitting cloak just a moment before doing the pogo to help yourself line it up, but I'm not sure how consistent that is. 
- You can use the chain as a visual cue for timing your dash -> cloak repress in the air. I like to dash and repress cloak just before it.

Craw Pogo 2 intricacies
So this is going to be a bit long, but bear with me. In the beggining you sprint on the ceiling up until the point of aggroing the second craw, but dont go too far to not make the first craw go to your right. After they are both on your left side, you should always be able to reach the higher platform with one pogo regardless of the craw that dives or at what time the dive happens. When im up there, i like to stand a little bit to the right of the ledge without jumping.

Now there are two scenarios that can happen, if the craw you hit is lower than the other one, its the good scenario (first clip), if not, its the bad scenario (second clip). For both skips i start with a jump and a pogo little after the higher craw passes the height of the ledge.

For the first clip, you should keep them both to your left for most of the climb, doing one pogo on the higher craw, then hit him again, followed by the other one, use a spear, then you should separate them to not get stuck under the platform.

For the second clip, you will do the pogo on the higher craw again, but this time youll pogo the lower one twice in a row, with a spear in the middle, this should separate them. Then youll just need to continue the climb using one more spear (always use them when youre closer to the craw on the left to make sure you dont go too far to the right). In the clip i did two more spears, but its bc i didnt notice i was already high enough.

Adding a few notes on the setup for this skip originally posted by QAQ https://discord.com/channels/772964112908156938/1423484610150666442/1423484834499657788
This is what I personally look out for during this skip:
- After the sprint jump off the ledge, I use flew brew at the very peak of my jump. The reason why using flea brew in the first place is important, is because it allows you to move faster in the air and get more distance after the damage boost towards the final ledge grab.
- At this time I look at the flower position. This is the most important part, because it helps me decide in what position I want to heal and how much I want to space out the inputs. If you heal too early/too far from the flower's range, you won’t trigger its attack/you will trigger it too late. If you heal too late/too far into the flower's range, you won't have enough time to dash out of the heal before taking damage. Its range is like a circle, so you want to heal on the outer edge of that circle - earlier if the flower is lower, later if it's higher.
This is an example of a small streak with different rng.
1st, 4th, 5th, 7th attempts = I can see that the flower is pretty low. This is usually the easiest rng (and what seems to be the most common) as there is a pretty big room for when to heal. In this case I want to dash and then heal pretty much immediately, since being horizontally closer to the flower makes you get hit by its attack sooner. In attempts 1, 4, and 7 I could've even healed much earlier after the dash and it would've still worked.
2nd attempt= The flower seemed kind of in the middle, not too high, not too low. I heal slightly later after the dash so that I get in its range.
3rd, 6th attempts = The flower looked pretty far up, which is the hardest rng. I try to space out my inputs as much as possible, but not too much that I start to lose height. Example 6 was probably the tightest here.

Some strats for the Skarrgard at the entrance to Hunter's March (assuming you have Silkspear and nothing else)

The Skarrgard has 150 hp, so it's optimal to start the fight with at least 5/9 silk, though more than 5 doesn't hurt, and up to 7 can help. You can get 6 silk really easily/nearly optimally from the enemies on the way to the Skarrgard from Bell Beast (including 1 from the Silk Heart)

The Skarrgard has 3 possible moves - a swing, a jump, and a burrow. You can tell that the Skarrgard is going to swing when it draws back it's weapon, and you can pogo the Skarrgard between the two individual swings to get in an attack. The timing is fairly tight but very consistent after some practice (see attachment 1). For the jump and burrow, the visual indicator is the same - a slight crouch. However, there is an _audio_ indicator - if the Skarrgard growls before the attack, it will always be a jump. You should stay still if it is burrowing, and start moving towards the Skarrgard as soon as you _see_ that it is jumping, to avoid getting hit. It's very easy to get hit if you don't react quite quickly. It's nice to get into the habit of upslashing just before either of those attacks, both because niche timings can make it so that a regular slash will only hit the Skarrgard if it burrows and not if it jumps, and because the knockback from a regular slash makes it easier to get hit on a jump. Very rarely, the timings make it so that you have to do a minihop before the upslash to hit the Skarrgard on either attack. Attachments 2 and 3 are examples of what a jump and burrow should each look like.

# Cocoon Skip Skip Guide

Shoutouts to @Fallen and @InfiniteFun for discovery/setup help

There's a few different setups for this trick,** however this is the best universal one from testing**. 

Skip seems to be unaffected by fps, tested between 50-600fps. Maintaining height is especially difficult below 60fps.

Chalamet skip can be done without room reload and saves anywhere from about 0.7-2.7s depending on the rng. **Agro 2 pogo - THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RNG TO LEARN**
Fastest rng by a lot. Saves 2.5s and loses the least to miss. You sometimes have to delay a bit more than others. Basically, just agro him, walk right, and try to get 2 high fast pogos on him as he's rising. Chalamet tries to stay a specific distance from you, so use it to your advantage. __Clips 1 and 2 will have this.__

**Other agro rngs/strats**
-Instead of 2 pogo (especially at medium distances) you can go for a spear stall with 3-4 pogos. Both can go either direction __Clips 3 and 4 show this.__
-When he's too far to reach with a pogo, you can dash pogo pogo, shown in __Clip 5__ *This rng is noticeably riskier than others but is extremely fast. Bailing and doing room reload isn't a bad idea either.* 

**Non agro rngs**
This is kind of the wild west. He can be pretty unpredictable with his movement and some of these save under a second. Bailing is reasonable. 
-Clip 6: Can do the first or second version depending on his drift. Saves 1-1.5s
